messages:
liam: Heads-up: after rolling NCCL 3.0.0 to us-west canaries we see persistent collective hangs on several A100 nodes. Started ~2050001234.

anya: ugh, saw the alert. which clusters? can we pin it to a driver mismatch?

liam: us-west1-gpu-pool (mostly v100/a100 mix), ~12% of capacity showing allreduce timeouts. stack traces show ncclTimeoutError and processes stuck in ncclAllReduce.

infra-bot: [ALERT] collective_timeout_rate > 5% in us-west1-gpu-pool (p95 latency +400ms, failed collectives 82 over 10m)

mike: do we have a repro? small repro would help. also what's the kernel/driver matrix on those nodes?

deepa: quick cost note: our immediate backfill plan (route jobs to single-GPU fallbacks) will increase per-request cost ~1.6x due to reduced batching.

liam: repro attached below — simple script using our microbench harness.

liam: ```
# run on two 4-GPU nodes
python microbench/allreduce.py --size 16M --reps 100 --backend nccl
# hangs after ~20 iters
``` 

sarah: behavior looks like sticky P2P fail. On a few nodes `nvidia-smi topo -m` shows unexpected NVLINK missing links after driver probed.

anya: possible workaround: set NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS to force socket fallback, or set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 to avoid IB path for now. Both will hurt perf but may restore reliability quickly.

mike: can we hot-fix runtime to set those envs for affected pools only? then schedule canary to confirm.

deepa: if we do that, we should measure token cost delta and surface in the console so customers get transparent impact.

liam: short-term mitigation options ranked:
1) set NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS on us-west GPU nodes (fast)
2) cordon problem nodes and fall back to single-GPU scheduling (moderate ops)
3) rollback NCCL to 2.14 (requires driver/kernel compatibility checks & longer window)

anya: rollback risk: some newer kernels/driver combos we rely on for GPU thermals were tested only with nccl3 in the staging matrix. need confirmation from eng-infra.

mike: propose plan: implement (1) cluster-wide env change via telemetry-config for us-west canaries, run 60m smoke, if no regressions then expand. simultaneously start full fleet audit for driver+kernel combos.

sarah: I'll run the audit and post matrix. quick query: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=us-west1-gpu -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}:{.status.nodeInfo.kernelVersion}:{.status.nodeInfo.kubeletVersion}
{end}'` helps but driver version not in nodeInfo — need daemonset to report `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv`.

deepa: ops question: if we do (1), what's the expected perf regression? estimate p50 token latency +10-30%, throughput -15-35% depending on model.

liam: agree. we'll communicate to support/ps about degraded throughput and recommend rate-limits for heavy customers.

anya: action items:
- liam: push NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS to us-west canaries (5 nodes) & monitor (ETA 30m)
- sarah: run fleet driver/kernel audit and post matrix (ETA 2h)
- mike: prepare rollback steps for nccl 2.x and driver compatibility checklist (ETA 4h)
- deepa: estimate customer cost delta + update status page blurb (ETA 1h)

liam: starting change now. ping here when smoke is green or if we see regressions :thumbsup: 

infra-bot: [CHANGE] NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS applied to pool us-west1-gpu-pool-canary by liam at 2050001245

sarah: initial smoke looks promising, failed collectives dropped to 1 in 10m. continuing 60m watch.

mike: thanks. keep notes for postmortem; we'll decide whether to roll forward this policy to all pools vs a proper rollback.

deepa: noted. adding customer communication draft to #support.

liam: closing loop—if nothing spikes in 60m we expand to remaining canaries, then schedule a controlled rollout with traffic shaping.

sarah: will also instrument kernel/driver event counters to catch nvlink flaps automatically.

mike: thx all, great triage.
